newsitem.title: USA: Sun-Diamond banned from selling to goverment.
newsitem.headline: Sun-Diamond banned from selling to goverment.

text.p: The Agriculture Department Monday officially barred the fruit concern Sun-Diamond Growers of California from selling to the government for three years because of its recent criminal convictions for giving illegal gifts to a former Clinton cabinet member.

Sun Diamond was convicted this fall in federal court on eight criminal counts that included illegal gratuities to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy in 1993 and 1994 and illegal campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry.

The charges arose out of the government's two-year special investigation of the former Agriculture secretary, who resigned in 1994 amid accusations he took illegal gifts and favours from companies the department regulated.

The Agriculture Department proposed the ban in October and said it acted Monday to make it official after reviewing Sun-Diamond's appeal. It said it may consider shortening the bar "once sufficient evidence exists that Sun-Diamond has rehabilitated its business integrity and honesty."
Officials at the Pleasanton, Calif.-based agricultural cooperative were not immediately available for comment.

Sun-Diamond is owned by five member cooperatives which are in turn owned by about 4,500 farmers. The Sun-Diamond affiliates rank as the nation's largest growers of raisins, prunes, other dried fruits and nuts.

Earlier this month, the department said the affiliates should also be barred from federal food purchase programmes for up to three years because they failed to correct Sun-Diamond's business practices. The grower groups are appealing the proposed ban.
Sun-Diamond sells products to the Defence Department for government comissaries and military cafeterias. Data on how much the Pentagon buys from the cooperative was unavailable.
The department said the bar was effective as of Oct. 4 when it was first proposed.
